exceptions.justification: repo-contract never bundles this tool; the consumer installs and trusts it as their own devDependency, and repo-contract's preset spawns it with exactly the flags shown in this preset's run: array. `attw --pack . --format json` runs `npm pack` on the local directory and analyzes the resulting local tarball's type-resolution -- it does not download anything from the npm registry (that is the `attw <package-name>` form, not used here). `npm pack` runs the package's own `prepack`/`postpack` lifecycle scripts, which for a consumer are their own configured scripts, a capability they already hold. `--format json` writes to stdout.

repo-contract never bundles this tool; the consumer installs and trusts it as their own devDependency, and repo-contract's preset spawns it with exactly the flags shown in this preset's run: array. `commitlint --from <sha> --to <sha>` reads git commit messages in the given range (via a local git invocation) and lints them against the resolved config. Config resolution (`extends`) resolves only from `node_modules` (`@commitlint/config-conventional` is a devDependency here), never a remote source. No network request; output to stdout.

repo-contract never bundles this tool; the consumer installs and trusts it as their own devDependency, and repo-contract's preset spawns it with exactly the flags shown in this preset's run: array. `eslint <path> --format json` makes no network request. Config and plugin resolution (`extends`, shareable configs, plugins) resolves only from `node_modules`, never a URL; every plugin is a consumer-chosen devDependency visible in a package.json diff. A loaded plugin runs as ordinary Node code during the lint pass, the same trust boundary as any installed dependency. `--format json` writes to stdout only.

repo-contract never bundles this tool; the consumer installs and trusts it as their own devDependency, and repo-contract's preset spawns it with exactly the flags shown in this preset's run: array. `linkinator <start> --recurse --format json --skip node_modules` exists to make HTTP requests: it issues GET requests to every URL found in this repository's own committed docs content, to detect broken links. It sends no repository data anywhere -- it only requests URLs already present in the repo. This is the deliberate, documented network exception ADR 0007's Decision section calls out by name. `--format json` writes to stdout.

repo-contract never bundles this tool; the consumer installs and trusts it as their own devDependency, and repo-contract's preset spawns it with exactly the flags shown in this preset's run: array. `npm audit --omit=dev --json` is the one command here that inherently makes a network request: it sends the production dependency tree (package names and versions only -- no source code, no auth) to the configured npm registry as a bulk advisory query and receives back known advisories. The subcommand is `audit` (read-only), verified against npm's documentation to not be `publish`/`install`/etc. This is exactly, and only, what a dependency-advisory check must do.
